stx.dry.title: Dry run: what happens next
stx.warn.layout-mismatch: This group has a different layout than the rest of the pool, so the pool is only as safe as its weakest group.
stx.warn.stripe-weakens: Adding a single striped disk means losing that one disk loses the whole pool. Big yikes.
stx.warn.not-ssd: That's a spinning hard drive. Speed boost drives only help when they're SSDs.
stx.warn.special-permanent: A metadata drive becomes part of the pool for good: it can't be taken out later, and if it dies the pool dies.
stx.warn.log-single: One write boost drive is fine, but two (mirrored) is safer if the power cuts out.
stx.boot.title: Boot drive
stx.boot.subtitle: The drive NoCapOS runs from. Kept apart from your storage pools so it's never touched by accident.
stx.boot.stateText.good: Two drives hold the same system. If one dies, NoCapOS keeps running and still boots from the other.
stx.boot.stateText.bad: The other drive is carrying the system solo right now. Swap in a new drive so you're protected again.
stx.boot.stateText.single: If this drive fails, NoCapOS stops until it's reinstalled. A mirror keeps a live second copy.
stx.boot.why.not-zfs: Your system drive uses a regular filesystem, and that can't be turned into a mirror safely while it's running. To get a mirrored boot drive, reinstall and pick "ZFS mirror" in the installer. Until then: keep backups and watch the drive's health here.
stx.boot.why.pi: The Pi's firmware only boots from one card or drive, so a second drive can't take over by itself. Keep a backup of the system card instead.
stx.boot.why.sd: The system runs from an SD or eMMC card, which can't be mirrored to another drive. Back up the card instead.
stx.boot.why.arch: Boot mirrors work on 64-bit PCs and 64-bit ARM boards that start with UEFI. This one doesn't, so no mirror here.
stx.boot.why.unknown: NoCapOS couldn't figure out exactly which drive the system boots from, so it's not touching it. Safety first.
stx.boot.noCandidates: No free drive is big enough. Plug in one that's at least {size}.
stx.boot.resilver: Copying the system to the new drive: {pct}%
stx.boot.safe: Pool actions never list these drives, so you can't erase the system by mistake.
stx.boot.lead: Pick a free drive that's at least {size}. It gets the same layout as your boot drive, joins the system mirror and gets its own bootloader.
stx.boot.step.copy: Copy the boot drive's partition layout onto the new drive
stx.boot.step.join: Add it to the system mirror ({pools})
stx.boot.step.efi: Set up its own EFI partition and bootloader, so either drive can start the server
stx.boot.step.bios: Install the bootloader on it, so either drive can start the server
stx.boot.step.resilver: ZFS copies the system over in the background; keep using the server meanwhile
stx.boot.erase: It becomes the second half of your boot mirror.
stx.boot.started: Boot mirror set up, copying in the background
stx.boost.title: Speed boost drives
stx.boost.lead: Fast SSDs that make a pool of hard drives feel quicker. Optional, and only worth it with SSDs.
stx.boost.blurb.cache: Keeps hot files on the SSD so reads fly. Safe: if it dies, nothing is lost.
stx.boost.blurb.log: Speeds up apps that wait for every write to land (databases, VMs).
stx.boost.blurb.special: Puts folder info and tiny files on SSD. Needs two drives; can't be removed later.
stx.boost.erase: They join pool {pool} as speed boost drives.
stx.boost.removeTitle: Remove this drive from the pool?
stx.boost.removeBody: The pool keeps all its files; it just gets a bit slower.
stx.scrub.explain: A scrub reads every block and checks it against its checksum. If something went bad, ZFS heals it from the good copy automatically.
stx.arc.title: RAM cache
stx.arc.lead: ZFS keeps recently used data in spare RAM so reads skip the disk.
stx.arc.hits: {pct}% of reads come straight from RAM
stx.expand.hint: After swapping every disk for a bigger one, this lets the pool grow into the new space.
stx.expand.done: Pool grown into any new space
stx.spin.title: Spin down
stx.spin.lead: Let idle hard drives sleep to save power and noise. They wake up when you open a file (a few seconds' wait).
stx.crypt.title: Encrypted folders
stx.crypt.lead: Locked with your passphrase. NoCapOS never saves it, so nobody can open these without it, not even with the disks in hand.
stx.crypt.locked: Locked, files are hidden and encrypted
stx.crypt.name: Name
stx.crypt.passHint: At least 8 characters. A short sentence is easy to remember and hard to guess.
stx.crypt.forget: Forget the passphrase and the files are gone for good. Nobody can reset it, not even an admin.
stx.snap.title: Snapshots
stx.snap.subtitle: Instant save points, {size} held in total
stx.snap.lead: A snapshot freezes a folder in time in a split second. It only takes space for what changes afterwards.
stx.snap.empty: No datasets yet. Create a pool first.
stx.snap.schedule: Automatic snapshots, how many to keep:
stx.snap.schedHint: 0 turns that kind off. Older automatic snapshots are deleted once there are more than you keep; the ones you take by hand are never touched.
stx.snap.rollbackWarn: {name} goes back to how it was on {when}.
stx.snap.rollbackLoss: Everything changed since then is lost, and newer snapshots are deleted. To grab just a few files, use Browse or Clone instead.
stx.snap.readOnly: Snapshots are read-only, so nothing here can be changed by accident.
stx.snap.emptyFolder: This folder was empty back then.
stx.snap.cloneLead: Makes a new, editable folder that starts out exactly like the snapshot. Instant, and it takes no extra space until you change it.
stx.mounts.title: Shares & mounts
stx.mounts.subtitle: USB drives, network drives and cloud accounts, all in one spot
stx.mounts.noUsb: No USB drives plugged in. Plug one in and it shows up here and in Files.
stx.mounts.noNet: No network drives yet. Add them in Files → Network.
stx.mounts.cloudLead: Open a connected cloud account as a folder. Files stream on demand, nothing is copied until you open it.
stx.mounts.noCloud: No cloud accounts yet. Connect one in Files → Cloud.
stx.flex.title: Flexible array
stx.flex.lead: Mix any sizes, add one drive at a time, each file lives whole on one disk and parity has your back.
stx.flex.how: Every data drive keeps its own filesystem, so each file sits whole on one drive. One folder shows them all together. Parity drives (as big as your biggest data drive) refresh nightly and can rebuild a dead drive. If more drives die than you have parity, you only lose what was on those drives.
stx.flex.off: This is a preview and it's switched off on this server. Whoever runs it can turn it on.
